source_description: Lake Tahoe is a large freshwater lake in the Sierra Nevada of the United States. At a surface elevation of 6,225 ft (1,897 m), it is located along the border between California and Nevada, west of Carson City. Lake Tahoe is the largest alpine lake in North America. Its depth is 1,645 ft (501 m), making it the deepest in the United States after Crater Lake (1,945 ft (593 m)). Additionally, Lake Tahoe is the sixth largest lake by volume in the United States at 122,160,280 acre·ft (150,682,490 dam3), behind the five Great Lakes. The lake was formed about 2 million years ago and is a part of the Lake Tahoe Basin with the modern lake being shaped during the ice ages. It is known for the clarity of its water and the panorama of surrounding mountains on all sides. The area surrounding the lake is also referred to as Lake Tahoe, or simply Tahoe. More than 75% of the lake's watershed is national forest land, comprising the Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit of the United States Forest Service. Lake Tahoe is a major tourist attraction in both Nevada and California. It is home to a number of ski resorts, summer outdoor recreation, and tourist attractions. Snow and skiing are a significant part of the area's economy and reputation. Mountain and lake scenery are attractions throughout the year. The Nevada side also includes large casinos. name: Lake Hydra
review_id: commons:Dutch Springs (Lake Hydra) Quarry, Hanoverville Road, Bethlehem, PA (52403094274).jpg
creator: Warren LeMay from Chicago, IL, United States
label: Surface view
alt: Lake Hydra — surface view, as described by the source.
source_description: Beginning as a limestone quarry supplying limestone to a nearby cement plant in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania during much of the 20th Century, the industrial decline experienced by the rust belt during the 1960s and 1970s saw the closure of this former quarry in the mid-1970s, which subsequently flooded with a combination of storm runoff and groundwater. By 1980, the quarry had filled deep enough to make it a suitable scuba diving spot, with it opening to the public as Dutch Springs, operated by Stuart and Jane Wells Schooley, with an open water scuba diving facility, aqua park, and adventure course being located on the property around the quarry. The quarry operated until 2022, when the land was sold to a warehouse development, with the former owners being paid millions for the 95 acres of land so a development company could build two massive warehouses on the parts of the property not occupied by the quarry, with a proposal to fence the quarry off and leave it unused. However, due to the high-quality freshwater conditions in the quarry, a movement was started by divers in multiple parts of the Northeastern United States to prevent its closure. The movement succeeded in two local dive shop owners being donated the land by the developer, which will remain open for more limited open water scuba diving, under the name Lake Hydra. This photo was taken on Memorial Day Weekend in 2022, one of the last weekends Dutch Springs was open.

source_description: English: The Blue Grotto (Maltese: Taħt il-Ħnejja) is a number of sea caverns on the south coast of Malta, east of the fishermen's harbour Wied iż-Żurrieq. Wied iz-zurrieq is in the village of Qrendi and the blue grotto cave located within the Qrendi village as per Local Council Act 1993 It is located right across from the small uninhabited islet of Filfla.[1] Every day from sunrise until about 1 pm a unique sight can be observed here. The location of the cave combined with the sunlight lead to the water mirroring showing numerous shades of blue. Several caverns mirror the brilliant phosphorescent colours of the underwater flora; other caverns show a deep dark shade of blue. The Blue Grotto is a popular destination for tourists on the island of Malta with boat trips to visit the caves, scuba diving snorkeling and rock climbing being the most popular activities here. It also has some typical local restaurants that offer good food with stunning views. The location has been used many times by filmmakers.

The beautiful white sand beaches are too majestic that laying on the sand is not an exemption to your To-Do list while staying in the island. This barely 60 minute boat-ride from the main port of Baclayon to Pamilacan Island will surely make your vacation the most memorable you can ever have. The serene and tranquil place will surely give your soul a refreshing breath of air. A good place for soul searching it is. Not to mention how this white sand beaches will definitely give you a tempting feeling. More over, heading to the island will also give you a touch of magical experience when you can come across pod of dolphins taking their turns in getting your attention, spinning, jumping, and even just merely tagging along in your boat. An experience one can never forget and might as well give you the urge to come back to the island.

The day-use area offers a restroom and picnic area with tables, and the campground has RV sites, yurts and tent sites available year-round. It is named after the Scottish pioneer George Harris who settled here in the late 1880s to raise sheep and cattle. Harris Beach State Park is home to Bird Island (also known as Goat Island), which is reported to be the largest island off the Oregon Coast and is a National Wildlife Refuge. The island is also a breeding site for rare birds such as the tufted puffin. (oregonstateparks.org/index.cfm?do=parkPage.dsp_parkPage&a...) identity_status: English: Acropora hemprichii, Ras Katy, Sharm el-Sheikh, Red Sea, Egypt. This species of acroporid coral is found in shallow reefs in marine environments, occurs at depths of 3 to 15 m (9.8 to 49.2 ft), and lives for between 13 and 24 years. The species is listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List, and has a decreasing population. It's found in colonies of densely-packed branches, which are flat or upward-facing, are often more than 2 m (6.6 ft) wide, and can exist without the presence of any other species. Acropora hemprichii is common but only found in a small area; the Gulf of Aden, the Red Sea, the Philippines, and the Indian Ocean. The guy in the top right corner is a blackside hawkfish (Paracirrhites forsteri) and the two guys hidding in the coral are yellow chromis (Chromis analis).
